title: The Setting That Was Converted: What QVariant Does to 3.7, to 3e9 and to the Word "no"

questions.question: A setting of 3.7 is read with QVariant(3.7).toInt(&ok). What do you get?
questions.explanation: It rounds, and ok means only that a conversion was done. QVariant(3e9).toInt() gave -1294967296, also with ok true.

questions.question: QVariant(-1).toUInt(&ok) gives what?
questions.explanation: The conversion wrapped and said it worked.

questions.question: What do QVariant(QString("no")).toBool() and QVariant(QString("abc")).toBool() give?
questions.explanation: Only the empty string, 0 and false are false. A setting safety = off leaves the safety on.

questions.question: setting_bool is given "yes", "OFF" and "maybe". What happens?
options: yes is true, OFF is false, and maybe is refused
questions.explanation: 13 of 13 spellings were read and 9 of 9 non-answers refused.

questions.question: setting_int refuses the double 3.7 and accepts the double 5.0. Why?
options: 3.7 would change in becoming an int, and 5.0 would not
questions.explanation: Only a whole number that fits is accepted. 13 of 13 conversions that would change the value were refused.

questions.question: Why are the tests that show QVariant's own conversions written as measurements?
options: They describe Qt 6.2, and other versions may convert some of these differently
questions.explanation: They are what was observed and not a promise. The continuous integration runs on other versions.
